title: tt pipeline spec
description: A declarative pipeline for `tt pipeline run (FILE|-)`: an ordered list of stages the ttd daemon executes, so one trigger returns one digest instead of costing the orchestrator a round-trip per task. This is data, not a scripting language — there are no variables, conditionals or loops, only the fixed stage shapes below. Each fanout task runs on its OWN freshly spawned worker (never a reused one, whose leftover context would bias the task); at the worker cap the remainder queue on the shared pool. Workers persist after the run — reclaim them with `tt pi popidle` or `tt pi rm <cs>`.

name.description: Label for this pipeline, used in the daemon's progress notes on stderr. Defaults to 'pipeline'.

retries.description: How many times a FAILING review gate may re-run the fanout stage that precedes it. 0 (the default) means a failed review ends the run with exit 1 and the reviewer's reason. Each retry re-dispatches the whole preceding fanout on fresh workers.

stages.description: Stages, executed in order. At least one fanout stage is required (a spec with only review stages has nothing to review). A review stage reads the results of the stage before it.

stage.description: Exactly one of `fanout` or `review` must be set.

fanout.description: Tasks dispatched in parallel, one fresh worker each. Scopes MUST be disjoint — tt cannot detect overlap, and two workers editing the same files (or the same build) will corrupt each other's work and each other's verification.

join.description: How the FINAL stage's results are printed. 'digest' (default) prints one lean line per result — id, status, duration, one-line summary — and keeps full bodies out of the orchestrator's context; pull one with `tt pi results <id>`. 'full' inlines every body. Only the last stage's join is used. Ignored when --json is passed.

label.description: Short name for this task, prepended to the prompt as 'LABEL: <label>' so the worker (and the digest) can identify it.

task.description: The full prompt body. Use tt's task contract — TASK / FILES or SCOPE / CHANGE / DO NOT / SUCCESS, plus VERIFY for code changes. The worker takes every field literally and cannot ask you a follow-up question, so state the scope and the success check explicitly.

review.description: A gate: ONE fresh worker is handed every result of the preceding stage and must return a verdict. tt appends the verdict instruction automatically — the reviewer is told to end with exactly `PIPELINE_PASS` or `PIPELINE_FAIL: <reason>`, and the LAST such line in its reply decides. A reviewer that returns neither counts as a failure. The verdict is evidence, never acceptance: the orchestrator still owns the final diff review.

prompt.description: What to check. State the pass bar concretely ('did each result do X and report Y') rather than asking for a general opinion — a vague reviewer passes everything.

fanout.label: auth
fanout.task:
TASK: Audit src/routes/auth.ts for missing authentication checks.
FILES / SCOPE: src/routes/auth.ts only. Read-only.
SUCCESS: a list of findings as file:line, or the exact words 'NO DEFECTS FOUND'.

fanout.label: billing
fanout.task:
TASK: Audit src/routes/billing.ts for missing authentication checks.
FILES / SCOPE: src/routes/billing.ts only. Read-only.
SUCCESS: a list of findings as file:line, or the exact words 'NO DEFECTS FOUND'.

review.prompt: You are a strict reviewer. For each report below, confirm it inspected the file it was assigned and returned either concrete file:line findings or the exact words 'NO DEFECTS FOUND'. A vague or off-scope report is a FAIL.
